narrative: Material PL1__M290AAB3 shows moderately variable demand (CV=0.259) averaging 990 units per working day with no significant trend over the observation period. Lead times are short (mean 1.59 days) but unstable (CV=0.529), making lead-time variability the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-based order quantity of 8,962 units and safety stock of 1,496 units achieves the 95% service level while reducing annual costs by ~94.8% versus the current SAP configuration of MOQ=200.
warnings: Current SAP order quantity (MOQ=200) is far below EOQ (8962); ordering costs are approximately 45x higher than optimal.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous review with EOQ order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is moderately variable with no trend, making a fixed reorder-point / fixed-quantity policy appropriate. EOQ minimizes the sum of ordering and holding costs given the high ordering cost relative to unit holding cost.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is not binding; post-replenishment stock (1,496 + 8,962 = 10,458 units) uses 71% of the 14,728-unit limit, leaving adequate headroom.
